steps.title: REVIEW AND REBUTTAL: ZERO-SHOT IN-CONTEXT ADVERSARIAL LEARNING FOR IMPROVING RE-SEARCH IDEATION

conclusion: The central contribution of this paper is the formalization of “zero-shot in-context adversarial learning” for LLMs, instantiated as a GAN-inspired minimax game over an implicit neighborhood of optimal answers and realized via a multi-agent, purely in-context interaction scheme for research ideation. According to the evidence, no prior work was found that already formulates this specific adversarial, zero-shot, in-context learning framework or its associated theory; the agent could not identify existing GAN-style formulations that keep the adversarial process entirely in context without parameter updates. Thus, the core methodological idea appears genuinely new among the examined literature. A secondary contribution is the relative quality ranking metric for open-ended generation. Here, Fu et al. (2023) already propose GPTScore, which similarly uses a generative LM plus aspect-specific prompts to automate evaluation, but their method is based on per-item likelihood scores, whereas this submission introduces a blind, comparative ranking protocol and a scalarization of the target’s relative position; this constitutes a partial but nontrivial extension. Overall, given that the main theoretical/methodological framework is not challenged by overlapping prior work and the evaluation metric is only partially overlapped, the paper’s novelty constitutes a genuine advance.

core_judgments: The framework fills a notable gap in the field by conceptually adapting adversarial learning to the context of LLM-driven idea generation, an area that has seen limited exploration.

The use of a peer review-inspired multi-agent setup to promote iterative improvement in idea generation represents a conceptually novel contribution, distinguishing the work from prior approaches that typically do not model such structured, adversarial interactions among LLM agents.

The paper’s novelty lies in its creative adaptation of adversarial learning principles and academic peer review dynamics to the automated ideation process, offering a fresh perspective and a promising direction for advancing LLM-based research support systems.

The paper’s novelty lies in its creative adaptation of adversarial learning principles and academic peer review dynamics to the automated ideation process, offering a fresh perspective and a promising direction for advancing LLM-based research support systems.
The novelty primarily lies in the creative integration and adaptation of existing ideas rather than the introduction of entirely new theoretical constructs.
The GAN-inspired framing, while innovative, is more metaphorical than rigorously mathematical, and the multi-agent system mimics established peer review dynamics in a new context.

Although the relative quality ranking metric is presented as a novel evaluation tool, a more thorough discussion of its relationship to existing metrics for open-ended text generation would strengthen the novelty claim, as it remains unclear whether similar approaches have been explored in prior literature.
